endpoints.name: firmware_info
endpoints.notes: Form body appid=137&project_no=<TR…>&version=<n>& android_version=<app version> (the app AES-signs params; the server also answers unsigned requests with a browser-like User-Agent — bare curl gets an nginx 403). Exercised live 2026-08-19, then harvested systematically the same day (~280 queries; 11 images archived locally with checksums, not committed): appid 137 serves firmware for 9 project codes; appid 140 answers "no data" for everything tried (likely reserved for an app whose project codes we don't know); all cid/pid-composite projects (TR2408R015_2x_*, TR2504R00x_3x_*, TR2601R0xx_4x_*, …) return "no data" even at range-base versions — bare TR2311R003_2 was the one exception and yielded a 1 MB .ufw. The queried version must clear a floor (version=1 returns "no data", ~100+ works). The server rate-limits aggressively (HTTP 429 after ~100 rapid queries; ~5 s spacing works). The app maps firmware-version ranges and 12 ledType-indexed project_no prefixes (TR2408R015_26_<cid><pid>, R2305R021_14_…, TR2509R022_26_…, etc.) to OTA projects; images download from images.heaton.com.cn only with Referer: https://manage.heaton.com.cn/.
endpoints.returns: JSON with firmware version, changelog and a download URL on images.heaton.com.cn

cloud.failure_mode: Loss of the downloadable clip-art/material library (api.e-toys.cn), of app config files and manuals (app.heaton.cn), and of firmware-update checks and image hosting (manage./images. heaton.com.cn). Everything else — power, brightness, modes, clock, text, DIY drawing, PNG/GIF upload, slot management — is local BLE and keeps working; the FOSS clients replace the app entirely. The panel itself has no internet path on BLE models and never contacts these hosts.
cloud.notes: BLE models have no radio but BLE; only the companion app talks to these hosts. Whether the app uploads telemetry or account data was not audited.

identity.notes: BLE address type (public vs random-static) is unverified; if the address rotates, re-resolve by scanning for the LED_BLE prefix / FA02 characteristic.

ble.notes: Name prefix confirmed in the app code and community docs. Fallback: connect and enumerate — the command characteristic 0000fa02-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb under service 000000fa-… identifies this family regardless of name.

identification.notes: The app filters scans on the advertised-name prefix "LED_BLE" (BleManager scan callback). The 0x00FA service / FA02 characteristic pair is the family fingerprint; some firmware revisions expose the notify characteristic as FA03, others as the vendor 128-bit UUID d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129601 (the app's default) — discover, don't hardcode.

device.manufacturer: Shenzhen Heaton Technology Co., Ltd. / TIRO (OEM; sold under dozens of storefront brands and marketplace SKUs)
device.name: iPixel Color LED Matrix Panel (TIRO/Heaton)
device.notes:
The ubiquitous AliExpress/Amazon "iPixel Color" flexible silicone RGB LED matrix panel / scrolling sign (5 V USB powered, often IP65, adhesive backing), sold for car rear windows, shop fronts and advertising tickers in many sizes: 32x16, 64x16, 96x16, 48x24, 64x20, 32x32, 64x64, and long strips up to 448x32 pixels. Known marketplace SKUs/brands include JTPD-03-011 (many sizes, "QYJSD" and other re-seller labels), HCZ-001 "Smart Car Screen" (~210x131 mm) and its 64x64 sibling HCZ-002 — all re-seller SKUs of the same OEM platform, all driven by the "iPixel Color" app. Query the panel for its real geometry (device-info response, below); marketplace listings are unreliable (one HCZ-001 listing claims "32x23", a size the platform does not support).
COMPANION APP: "iPixel Color" for Android (ipixelcolor.net credits Shenzhen Heaton Technology Co., Ltd.). Internally it shares a developer namespace with the sibling apps Magic Display, iPixel Pro and SDJ.
SAME OEM FAMILY as led-helmet-display.yaml ("TIRO FA02" family): same FA02 command characteristic, same length-prefixed framing convention, same JieLi BLE SoC platform with the bundled com.tiro.jlotalibrary / JieLi OTA SDK, same Heaton cloud backend. The opcode map and panel geometries differ (helmet = 12x48 turn-signal panel driven by the Shining Display app; this = general-purpose sign driven by iPixel Color), so the two specs share infrastructure but not command tables.
FAMILY BOUNDARY — do not conflate with CoolLED1248 / Juntong (coolledx-led-sign.yaml), LOY (FFF0 service), or the Quintic AES-128-ECB Shining Mask family: similar marketplace appearance, different apps, different framing. This family is identified by the FA02 write characteristic under the 00FA service and LED_BLE advertising names. No encryption or pairing appears anywhere in the command path — plain GATT writes (a "password" mechanism exists in the protocol for some firmware — see the password_flag note — but 255 = no password is the norm).
HARDWARE PLATFORM: JieLi BLE SoC; firmware images are JieLi OTA packages. Two formats observed in the 2026-08-19 harvest: the `*_ota_mi.bin` files are chip-key scrambled (no ASCII header, entropy 6.2-7.2 bits/byte, and all nine share the same scrambled 4-byte repeating prefix — consistent with JieLi chip-key XOR of a constant boot header), while the rarer `.ufw` files are JieLi JLUFW update containers with plaintext section strings (JLUFW, JLBTSDK, ble_app_ota.bin) — the appid-137 TR2311R003 .ufw carries AC695x / BR22 markers, i.e. JieLi AC695N. Some variants add a Wi-Fi radio (listings say "Bluetooth WiFi" and bundle an IR remote); the app contains a WifiSend interface, but BLE remains the primary and community-documented transport.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the GATT layout and the core command table — app-derived AND cross-verified against multiple working FOSS clients. MEDIUM for the bulk-upload windowing details and the screen-select opcode (two community sources disagree — see show_slot). LOW for the Wi-Fi variant path, the password mechanism, and factory-reset semantics.

pairing.notes: Plain GATT writes with no encryption and no pairing anywhere in the command path, independently confirmed by the ESPHome component for this family. The protocol does carry an optional password mechanism on some firmware, but its flag value of 255 means no password and that is what the panels ship with; a client should read the flag rather than assume either way.

credentials.notes: No credentials of any kind on BLE models: the panel speaks unauthenticated GATT. A password flag exists in the device-info response (255 = none); the password wire format is unverified.

factory_reset.effect: The clear command (opcode 0x8003, frame 04 00 03 80) is documented by the community clients as wiping all stored content from the panel's memory, including device settings — i.e. a software factory reset. Inferred from client behaviour, not observed by us on hardware; no physical button procedure was found in listings or the app.

steps.action: Write the clear frame (04 00 03 80) to the FA02 characteristic.
steps.notes: Community-documented as removing all stored screens and settings. Behaviour on the panel (reboot, LED signal, what survives) is unverified.

ble.pin_source: None — plain GATT writes. A per-device password mechanism exists (password_flag in the device-info response; 255 = no password) but its wire format is unverified.

methods.description: Scan for the LED_BLE name prefix, connect, enumerate services, locate FA02 (write) and FA03 or the vendor 128-bit notify characteristic, enable notifications via CCCD 0x2902, then send the time-sync/device-info command — the panel answers with its geometry and firmware info on the notify characteristic.

steps.expect: Panel advertises with an LED_BLE-prefixed name.

steps.action: Connect and discover services; locate characteristic 0000fa02-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (write / write-without-response) under service 000000fa-….
Enable notifications (CCCD 0x2902 = 01 00) on 0000fa03-… if present, else on d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129601. Command ACKs and the device-info response arrive here.
Send sync_time (opcode 0x8001 with the current time); the panel replies with its device-info record — byte 4 is the device-type byte that maps to panel geometry (see the command notes).

setup.notes: Nothing to provision: no Wi-Fi to join (BLE models), no account, no cloud. Power the panel on, scan, connect. Multiple FOSS clients do exactly this on real hardware.

rejoin.notes: No network to rebind. The usual connection failure is another central still holding the link — close the vendor app before connecting from another client.

testing.notes: Everything here comes from static analysis of the companion app ("iPixel Color"), live probes of the vendor cloud API on 2026-08-19, and several community open-source clients (pypixelcolor/iPixel-CLI, go-ipxl, ipixel-ctrl, ha-ipixel-color) that are reported to work on real panels. We did not capture BLE traffic or drive hardware ourselves; frames below are read out of the app's command builders and cross-checked against the community implementations, which agree.

entities.name: Display Power
entities.notes: Write-only channel; no state readback is documented, so a consumer must track what it sent rather than reading the panel back.

entities.name: Orientation
entities.notes: Four raw indices 0-3; the index-to-angle map is community-assumed — verify on hardware.

entities.name: DIY (Fun) Mode
entities.notes: Write-only channel; no state readback is documented, so a consumer must track what it sent rather than reading the panel back.

artifacts.description: Static analysis of the "iPixel Color" Android companion app (2026-08-19). Its BLE managers gave the LED_BLE scan filter, the 0x00FA service and the FA02 write characteristic; its send core gave the length-prefixed framing and the CRC32 over the payload; its options defaults gave the vendor 128-bit notify UUID; and its OTA layer — a wrapper around the JieLi OTA SDK — gave the 12 ledType-indexed OTA project_no prefixes and the appid 137 used against the vendor firmware API.

TR2104R003_02_47_ota_mi.bin — OTA image captured live from images.heaton.com.cn 2026-08-19 (Referer-gated). Chip-key scrambled, internals not analysed. One of eight captured; the other seven (sha256): TR2104R003_04_04 df999fea2595bb98d1b538c01229689154ce18bc01b2505fbc3640b6f67ba3db, TR2204R009_03_17 ee1646642bb4de971b03b014efc295bfc8b8e74e8f3ae78cf12ef6c535d156bf, TR2304R004_16_02 94b50062c5343cc61b9cd708a1932b74fa65233dfc4f9da96306b17e61029bd3, TR2304R009_10_05 f5b54285c86a84b213d3cff2cb698123c07c3bffbdd4d021b7ef23b550e5e93c, TR2305R017_07_02 aaec2375b86023ce334cb64b288992dec5d430303fdd9440e5f586709347bda1, TR2305R021_08_05 89b8dca9495d8498540977789e053654b69d42ea7549d1bb3bedd381e680c6c3, TR2310R004_13_03 f0132c7e468af2e10f3353da96a78ad294a784e0cca123697f496def1ee6a68f. A same-day systematic harvest (2026-08-19, ~280 queries against appids 137/140/141) archived 11 images total locally with checksums (referenced, not committed); 8 overlap this list, 3 are new: TR2304R004_05_10_ota_mi.bin (appid 137, TR2304R004-05 v510, scrambled like the others), TR2311R003_17_03_000106.ufw (appid 137, TR2311R003_2 v1703 — a JieLi JLUFW container whose plaintext section strings mark it AC695N / BR22 platform, internal project TR2311R003), and TR2411R014-02.ufw (appid 141 helmet family — see led-helmet-display.yaml). Which project code maps to which panel size is unknown — read the version via the device-info response on real hardware.
Python client; command frames, windowed PNG/GIF upload, and the device-type-to-geometry map cross-checked against this spec. Reported working on real panels.

Home Assistant integration + protocol documentation (itself derived from yyewolf/go-ipxl and sdolphin-JP/ipixel-ctrl). Source of the 0x8007 select-screen variant and the anchor-flag table (0x01 left, 0x02 right, 0x10 top, 0x20 bottom, 0x00 centre).
ESPHome component; independent confirmation that the protocol needs no encryption or pairing.

covers: clock faces and time sync, fun/DIY pixel mode, music-rhythm modes
PNG image and GIF animation upload (client-side resize to panel geometry), 9 content slots, slot select/delete
text display (rendered client-side to an image and uploaded — there is no separate text wire format in the community clients)
not_covered: firmware update checks and image hosting (cloud-hosted; a captured image can in principle be flashed without the cloud via the JieLi OTA service)
Wi-Fi variant control path (app has a WifiSend interface; undocumented)
local_access.summary: The panel speaks plain unauthenticated BLE GATT as shipped; the cloud is an optional content store, not a control path. Multiple working FOSS clients exist (pypixelcolor/iPixel-CLI in Python, go-ipxl in Go, an ESPHome component, and a Home Assistant HACS integration), so the device is already usable cloud-free today. A minimal client is 5-byte writes to FA02 plus one notify subscription.

remaining_unknowns: Notify characteristic: FA03 vs vendor 128-bit d44bc439-… is firmware-revision dependent; ACK payload format not fully documented
show_slot opcode discrepancy (0x8008 7-byte vs 0x8007 5-byte) — likely firmware-revision dependent, untested by us
Device-type byte to geometry map has collisions (139/141 both 96x32, 140/142 both 128x32); treat as approximate
Password mechanism: wire format unknown (password_flag 255 = none is the norm)
Wi-Fi variant control path (WifiSend interface in the app) is undocumented
clear (0x8003) exact effect — what survives a wipe — is inferred from client docs, not observed
Which OTA project code maps to which panel size; per-size cid/pid pairs come from the device-info response at connect time
CRC32 byte order in the upload header is little-endian per pypixelcolor; an older community document shows big-endian packing — verify on hardware if uploads fail CRC
JieLi OTA image de-scrambling (chip-series key) if firmware internals are wanted

clear.advanced_reason: Community-documented as a full wipe of stored screens AND device settings — a software factory reset. Recovery is re-uploading your content from a client.
clear.description: Erase all stored content and settings (opcode 0x8003, no payload)

fun_mode_off.description: Disable DIY ('fun') mode (set_fun_mode with state=0, opcode 0x0104).

fun_mode_on.description: Enable DIY ('fun') mode (set_fun_mode with state=1, opcode 0x0104).

power_off.description: Display power OFF (set_power with state=0, opcode 0x0107).

power_on.description: Display power ON (set_power with state=1, opcode 0x0107).

send_gif.description: Upload an animation (opcode 0x0003). Identical windowing to send_png except the opcode bytes are 03 00 and the tail byte before the slot is 0x02 (PNG uses 0x00). GIFs are re-encoded client-side (palette mode, per-frame durations). Windowed upload with the same per-window header layout as send_png, so it has no single template either.

send_png.description: Upload a static image (opcode 0x0002). The image is resized client-side to the panel geometry and encoded as PNG (RGB, no palette). Sent in ~12 KB windows; EVERY window is a complete frame: u16-LE length (= frame length + 2), then 02 00, option byte (0x00 first window, 0x02 continuation), u32-LE total PNG size, u32-LE CRC32 of the PNG data, tail bytes 00 <save_slot> (save_slot 0 = show only, 1-9 = store to slot), then the window's chunk of PNG data. Each window requires an ACK on the notify characteristic before the next is sent. Windowed upload: there is no single template — build each window from the header layout above.

level.notes: Percent 0-100 per the community clients; the vendor app's internal scale was not separately traced.

set_clock_mode.description: Show a clock face (opcode 0x0106). Style 0-8, plus 12/24 h, show-date toggle and the current date.

set_fun_mode.description: Enable/disable DIY ('fun') mode for direct pixel control (opcode 0x0104)

orientation.notes: 0/90/180/270-degree index; the index-to-angle map is community-assumed, verify on hardware.

set_pixel.description: Set one pixel to an RGB colour while in DIY mode (opcode 0x0105)

set_rhythm_mode_2.description: Alternate rhythm mode (opcode 0x0200): animated style 0-1, animation speed 0-7

show_slot.description: Display a stored content slot (1-9; empty slots are skipped). OPCODE DISCREPANCY: pypixelcolor uses the 7-byte frame below (opcode 0x8008), while the ha-ipixel-color documentation records a 5-byte select-screen frame 05 00 07 80 <slot> (opcode 0x8007). Both are reported working; likely firmware-revision dependent. Try 0x8008 first, fall back to 0x8007.

sync_time.description: Sync the clock AND query device info (opcode 0x8001 — the same frame serves both: the panel answers on the notify characteristic with its device-info record). Byte 4 of the response is the device-type byte: 128=64x64, 129=32x32, 130=32x16, 131=64x16, 132=96x16, 133=64x20, 134=128x32, 135=144x16, 136=192x16, 137=48x24, 138=64x32, 139/141=96x32, 140/142=128x32 per the community map (some entries collide; treat the map as approximate and measure when in doubt). Byte 10 of the response is the password flag (255 = no password).

characteristics.name: Display Command
characteristics.notes:
Frame layout (app builders and all community clients agree):

  bytes 0-1: total frame length N, little-endian u16 (covers
             the whole frame including these two bytes)
  bytes 2-3: opcode, little-endian u16. Across the opcodes
             this spec records, the HIGH byte is the group and
             the LOW byte is the command within it: 0x80xx is
             display and system (sync_time, clear, brightness,
             orientation, screen select, show_slot), 0x01xx is
             content and mode (delete_slot, DIY mode, set_pixel,
             clock mode, power), 0x00xx is upload (send_png,
             send_gif) and 0x02xx is rhythm. Sharing a LOW byte
             relates nothing — 0x8004 brightness and 0x0104
             DIY mode, 0x8001 sync_time and 0x0201 rhythm,
             0x8003 clear and 0x0003 send_gif are unrelated
             pairs. The one genuinely related pair recorded
             here, show_slot 0x8008 and the screen-select
             0x8007, shares the HIGH byte. This is a reading of
             17 observed opcodes, not a documented scheme:
             do NOT derive an unlisted opcode from it.
  bytes 4..: payload

Written as raw bytes; large writes (image uploads) are split into ~12 KB windows, each window a complete frame with its own length prefix and header, and each window ACKed on the notify characteristic before the next is sent.

characteristics.name: Display Notify (community firmware)
characteristics.notes: Command ACKs and the device-info response. Some firmware revisions instead expose the vendor 128-bit UUID d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129601 (the app's default); clients should enumerate and subscribe to whichever notify characteristic the panel actually has. ACK payload format is not fully documented (a short echo/status frame).

services.name: iPixel Command Service
services.notes: 16-bit service 0x00FA per the app's BLE manager and community docs. All display commands are written to FA02; feedback (command ACKs, device-info response) arrives on the notify characteristic.

characteristics.name: JieLi OTA Write
characteristics.notes: OTA data channel. Wire format is the JieLi OTA protocol's own (SDK-internal), not traced here.

services.name: JieLi OTA Service
services.notes: Standard JieLi firmware-update service (the app bundles the JieLi OTA SDK via com.tiro.jlotalibrary, with the JieLi OTA notify UUID 003784cf-f7e3-55b4-6c4c-9fd140100a16 and ae00-service patterns — the same OTA machinery as led-helmet-display.yaml). Presence on this panel family is inferred from the app, not confirmed on-air. Firmware images are JieLi OTA packages, chip-key scrambled (no ASCII header); eight current images were captured from the vendor cloud (see sources).
